This section provides structured literature reviews and source collections across four core biomechanical and control topics foundational to the AffineDrift modeling framework.

## Core Review Topics

::: {.resource-grid}
::: {.resource-card}
### [Interaction Forces in the Golf Swing](research-review-interaction-forces.html)

Examines how inter-segment joint reaction forces and velocity-dependent coupling terms (Coriolis and centrifugal) transfer energy across kinematic chains during rotational sport movements.

[Read Interaction Forces Review](research-review-interaction-forces.html){.resource-link}
:::

::: {.resource-card}
### [Induced Acceleration Analysis](research-review-induced-acceleration-analysis.html)

Evaluates dynamic decomposition techniques (IAA and generalized force contributions) that quantify how individual muscle actuators and contact reaction forces accelerate individual system coordinates.

[Read Induced Acceleration Review](research-review-induced-acceleration-analysis.html){.resource-link}
:::

::: {.resource-card}
### [Shaft Flexibility in Golf Swing Dynamics](research-review-shaft-flexibility.html)

Analyzes modal shaft bending, torsional deflection, and elastic strain energy recovery across the swing cycle, evaluating empirical evidence against rigid-body vs. flexible multibody approximations.

[Read Shaft Flexibility Review](research-review-shaft-flexibility.html){.resource-link}
:::

::: {.resource-card}
### [Baseball Pitching Biomechanics](research-review-baseball-pitching.html)

Presents cross-sport comparative biomechanics analyzing multi-segment rotational sequencing, kinetic chain transfer, and shoulder internal rotation mechanics in high-velocity throwing.

[Read Baseball Pitching Review](research-review-baseball-pitching.html){.resource-link}
:::
:::

## Methodological Criteria

Each review is organized around four core analytical standards:

1. **Explicit Problem Formulation:** Stating the exact dynamical question addressed in the empirical and theoretical literature.
2. **Empirical vs. Modeling Distinctions:** Rigorously separating direct sensor measurements (motion capture, force plates, EMG) from model-derived estimates (inverse dynamics, optimization outputs).
3. **Evidence Boundaries:** Identifying experimental validation envelopes, sample sizes, and unmodeled boundary conditions.
4. **Control-Affine Relevance:** Mapping empirical findings directly to the control-affine equations of motion $\dot{x} = f(x) + G(x)u$.
